Source comparison · The original five-point calculation and video links

A second dataset for an independent calculation

This is the original teaching source’s five-point example, separate from the retailer’s eight market-weeks. X and Y here have generic units. Do not combine the observations or substitute these numbers into the retailer’s forecast. Calculations below keep full precision before rounding and correct the source’s rounded arithmetic.

  1. Fit: x̄ = 3, ȳ = 6, Sxx = 10, Sxy = 7. Thus b = 7/10 = 0.7 and a = 6 − 0.7 × 3 = 3.9.
  2. Partition and noise: SST = 18, SSE = 0.36 + 2.89 + 0 + 7.29 + 2.56 = 13.1, SSR = 4.9. Residual df = 5 − 2 = 3, s² = 13.1/3, s ≈ 2.089657 and R² = 4.9/18 ≈ 0.272222.
  3. Slope: SE = s/√10 ≈ 0.660808. For H₀: β = 0, t ≈ 1.059310, two-sided p ≈ 0.367198. With t critical 3.182446 and 3 df, the 95% slope CI is [−1.402985, 2.802985]. F = (4.9/1)/(13.1/3) ≈ 1.122137 = t², with the same upper-tail p. Do not reject zero slope at 5%; this is not proof of no relationship.
  4. Intercept: SE = s√(1/5 + 3²/10) ≈ 2.191651. The zero-null t ≈ 1.779481 has two-sided p ≈ 0.173208; the 95% CI is [−3.074811, 10.874811]. x = 0 is outside the observed range.
  5. Two targets at x₀ = 6: fitted y = 8.1. Mean SE = s√(1/5 + (6 − 3)²/10) ≈ 2.191651; the pointwise mean CI is [1.125189, 15.074811]. New-response SE = s√(1 + 1/5 + (6 − 3)²/10) ≈ 3.028201; the PI is [−1.537086, 17.737086]. Both require the classical model, and the PI adds an independent new error. Six is beyond the observed 1–5 range: these formulas do not protect against extrapolation failure.
Check: Reproduce both tail probabilities without a regression add-in

For the retailer’s manual worksheet, use =T.DIST.2T(ABS(U7),COUNT(A2:A9)-2) and =F.DIST.RT(U9,1,COUNT(A2:A9)-2). Both are about 0.00001443. Repeat with the five-point example’s t, F and 3 residual df: both are about 0.367198. Match the data, degrees of freedom and tails before comparing results.
